verses.sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच।
              ततो व्यूढेष्वनीकेषु समुत्क्रुष्टेषु मारिष।  ताड्यमानासु भेरीषु मृदंगेषु नदत्सु च ॥१॥
अनीकानां च संह्रादे वादित्राणां च निःस्वने।  प्रध्मापितेषु शंखेषु सन्नादे लोमहर्षणे ॥२॥
verses.english: When the soldiers uttered loud war-cries and musical instruments emitted tremendous din, when conchs were blown and horripilating roars were heard.

verses.sanskrit: अभिहारयत्सु शनकैर्मरतेषु युयुत्सुषु।  रौद्रे मुहूर्ते संप्राप्ते सव्यसाची व्यदृश्यत ॥३॥
verses.english: When the field slowly became over-spread with Bharata heroes desirous of battle and when the hour known as Roudra arrived, Savyasachin (Arjuna) made his appearance on the field of battle.

verses.sanskrit: बलानां वायसानां च पुरस्तात् सव्यसाचिनः। बहुलानि सहस्त्राणि प्राक्रीडंस्तत्र भारत ॥४॥
verses.english: Then, O Bharata, many thousands of ravens and crows flew sportively in front of Arjuna's car.
verses.bhavadeepa: तत इति ॥१॥ अभिहारयत्सु सन्नह्यमानेषु अभियुज्यमानेषु वा प्रहरत्स्विति केचित् ॥३॥

verses.sanskrit: मृगाश्च घोरसंनादाः शिवाश्चाशिवदर्शनाः।  दक्षिणेन प्रयातानामस्माकं प्राणदंस्तथा ॥५॥
सनिर्घाता ज्वलन्त्यश्च पेतुरुल्काः सहस्रशः।  चचाल च मही कृत्स्ना भये घोरे समुत्थिते ॥६॥
verses.english: Thousands of meteors, with harsh sounds and blazing tails, began to drop down; on the dreadful occasion, the whole Earth began to quake and tremble.

verses.sanskrit: विष्वग्वाताः सनिर्घाता रूक्षाः शर्करकर्षिणः। ववुरायाति कौन्तेये संग्रामे समुपस्थिते ॥७॥
verses.english: Dry winds accompanied by deep sounds and driving pebbles and gravel, began to blow when Kunti's son made his appearance before the commencement of the battle.

verses.sanskrit: नाकुलिश्च शतानीको धृष्टद्युम्नश्च पार्षतः।  पाण्डवानामनीकानि प्राज्ञौ तौ व्यूहतुस्तदा ॥८॥
verses.english: Then Shatanika the son of Nakula and Dhristadyumna the son of Prishata, these two warriors endued with great wisdom began to array in order the numerous divisions of the Pandavas.

verses.sanskrit: ततो रथसहस्त्रेण द्विरदानां शतेन च।  त्रिभिरश्वसहस्त्रैश्च पदातीनां शतैः शतैः ॥९॥
verses.english: Supported by a thousand cars, a hundred elephants, three thousand horses and ten thousand foot-soldiers and covering a part of the field measuring fifteen hundred bows, your son Durmarshana stationed himself in the very

verses.sanskrit: अध्यर्धमात्रे धनुषां सहस्रे तनयस्तव।  अग्रतः सर्वसैन्यानां स्थित्वा दुर्मर्षणोऽब्रवीत् ॥१०॥
अद्य गाण्डीवधन्वानं तपन्तं युद्धदुर्मदम्।  अहमावारयिष्यामि वेलेव मकरालयम् ॥११॥
verses.english: Like the banks resisting the waves of the swelling main, even I myself will this day hold in check the wielder of the Gandiva bow, that slayer of foes, that hero who is irrepressible in battle.

verses.sanskrit: अद्य पश्यन्तु संग्रामे धनञ्जयममर्षणम्।  विषक्तं मयि दुर्धर्षमश्मकूटमिवाश्मनि ॥१२॥
verses.english: Today let people see the irate and indomitable Dhananjaya collide with me, even like a mass of stone against another story mass.

verses.sanskrit: तिष्ठध्वं रथिनो यूयं संग्राममभिकांक्षिणः।  युध्यामि संहतानेतान् यशो मानं च वर्धयन् ॥१३॥
एवं ब्रुवन्महाराज महात्मा स महामतिः।  महेष्वासैर्वृतो राजन् महेष्वासो व्यवस्थितः ॥१४॥
ततोन्तक इव क्रुद्धः सवज्र इव वासवः।  दण्डपाणिरिवासह्यो मृत्युः कालेन चोदितः ॥१५॥
शूलपाणिरिवाक्षोभ्यो वरुणः पाशवानिव।  युगान्ताग्निरिवार्चिष्मान्प्रधक्ष्यन्वै पुनः प्रजाः ॥१६॥
क्रोधामर्षबलोद्धूतो निवातकवचान्तकः।  जयो जेता स्थितः सत्ये पारयिष्यन् महाव्रतम् ॥१७॥
verses.english: That slayer of the Nivatakavachas, inflamed with rage and swelling with his energies, the ever victorious Jaya attached to truth and intent on accomplishing his great vow.

verses.sanskrit: आमुक्तकवचः खड्गी जाम्बूनद‌किरीटभृत्।  शुभ्रमाल्याम्बरधरः स्वंग‌श्चारुकुण्डलः ॥१८॥
verses.english: Cased in mail and armed with a sword, graced with a golden diadem, decorated with garlands of white flowers and attired in white garments, his arms decked with charming Angadas and ears with resplendent ear-rings.

verses.sanskrit: रथप्रवरमास्थाय नरो नारायणानुगः।  विधुन्वन् ‌गाण्डिवं संख्ये बभौ सूर्य इवोदितः ॥१९॥
verses.english: Riding on his own best of chariots, the embodied Nara accompanied by Narayana, shaking his Gandiva bow in battle appeared shining and dazzling like the risen sun.

verses.sanskrit: सोग्रानीकस्य महत इषुपाते धनञ्जयः। व्यवस्थाप्य रथं राजञ्शंखं दध्मौ प्रतापवान् ॥२०॥
verses.english: Then Dhananjaya endued with great might, O king, stopping his chariot before the van of his troops where the thickest downpour of arrows was expected blew his conch.

verses.sanskrit: अथ कृष्णोऽप्यसंभ्रान्तः पार्थेन सह मारिष। प्राध्मापयत्पाञ्चजन्यं शंखप्रवरमोजसा ॥२१॥
तयोः शंखप्रणादेन तव सैन्ये विशांपते।  आसन् संहृष्टरोमाणः कम्पिता गतचेतसः ॥२२॥
verses.english: Then at that blare of the conchs, O ruler of men, the soldiers of your army had the hair of their body erect and they trembled and were confounded.

verses.sanskrit: यथा त्रस्यन्ति भूतानि सर्वाण्यशनिनिःस्वनात्।  तथा शंखप्रणादेन वित्रेसुस्तव सैनिकाः ॥२३॥
प्रसुस्रुवुः शकृन्मूत्रं वाहनानि च सर्वशः।  एवं सवाहनं सर्वमाविग्नमभवद्बलम् ॥२४॥
सीदन्ति स्म नरा राजन् शंखशब्देन मारिष।  विसंज्ञाश्चाभवन्केचित् केचिद्राजन् वितत्रसुः ॥२५॥
verses.english: O sire, O monarch, in consequence of the blare of those two conchs, all men were deprived of their strength. And some of our array the were filled with fear and some lost their consciousness.

verses.sanskrit: ततः कपिर्महानादं सह भूतैर्ध्वजालवैः।  अकरोद्व्यादितास्यश्च भीषयंस्तव सैनिकान् ॥२६॥
ततः शंखाश्च भेर्यश्च मृदंगाश्चानकैः सह।  पुनरेवाभ्यहन्यन्त तव सैन्यप्रहर्षणाः ॥२७॥
verses.english: Then conchs, horns, cymbals and Anakas, were sounded and blown for inspiring energy into your troops.

verses.sanskrit: नानावदित्रसंह्रादैः क्ष्वेडितास्फोटिताकुलैः।  सिंहनादैः समुत्कृष्टैः समाधूतैर्महारथैः ॥२८॥
verses.english: Then din thus produced, became mixed up with the din produced by various musical instruments, by the shouts of warriors and by the slappings of their armpits, by the war-cries of the great car-warriors, as they challenged one another.

verses.sanskrit: तस्मिंस्तु तुमुले शब्दे भीरूणां भयवर्धने।  अतीव हृष्टो दाशार्हमब्रवीत् पाकशासनिः ॥२९॥
verses.english: Thus when that tremendous din arose there din that enhanced the fear of the cowards the son of Pakashasani became filled with joy; and addressing the descendant of the Dasarha race, he then thus spoke.
